source_name: DLA Piper Hungary – Publications / Insights
why_relevant: Band 1 Hungary banking & finance practice within a firm that runs high-cadence, jurisdiction-tagged financial-services regulatory alert programmes (including EU payments and DORA series). Useful for early English framing of EU obligations landing on Hungarian institutions.

source_name: Katona & Partners Attorneys at Law – Hungarian payments commentary
why_relevant: Confirmed via the Mondaq Hungary finance & banking listing as a recurring contributor publishing the same payments-law article in Hungarian, English and German ('Euróval történő fizetés' / 'Payment in Euro' / 'Zahlung in Euro'). Trilingual output makes it an unusually good source for terminology mapping on payment obligations.

source_name: Lexology – Hungary financial services / banking regulation library
why_relevant: Aggregates Hungarian law-firm alerts and hosts recurring structured 'In-Depth' / 'In brief' country chapters on Hungarian banking regulation and consumer finance, authored by Hungarian practitioners. The country chapters give a dated, citable baseline of the regime that alerts then amend.

source_name: JD Supra – DORA / financial services topic feed
why_relevant: Third major law-firm alert aggregator; its topic feeds (DORA, crypto-assets, financial services industry) surface firm alerts that mention Hungarian implementation. Weaker on Hungarian-language content but useful for redundancy against Lexology/Mondaq paywalling.

source_name: CEE Legal Matters – Hungary
why_relevant: CEE legal-market trade publication carrying Hungarian legal news and firm-authored analysis, plus market intelligence on which firms handle which mandates. Doubles as an actor map: it reveals partner moves and practice launches that predict where future alerts will come from.

source_name: Legal 500 / Chambers & Partners – Hungary banking, finance and capital markets rankings
why_relevant: Directory rankings are the cleanest way to enumerate the full universe of Hungarian banking/finance interpreter firms (and the named partners who author alerts) before crawling each one. Chambers publishes downloadable Hungary PDFs listing every ranked firm by band.

source_name: Compliance/RegTech vendor advisories on Hungary (Copla, CyberUpgrade, Legal Nodes)
why_relevant: Non-law-firm compliance advisories that translate Hungarian applications of DORA and MiCA into operational obligation lists — including the useful 'Mini DORA' (Art. 16 simplified ICT risk framework) distinction for Hungarian financial enterprises, and confirmation that MNB is the sole MiCA authority under Act VII of 2023. Lower authority than law firms but often clearer on scoping and dates; must always be verified against the primary instrument.

source_name: EY Law Hungary (IFLR1000 profile as entry point)
why_relevant: EY was the one Big Four firm for which no Hungarian financial-regulatory newsletter surfaced in either language during this pass; the IFLR1000 profile confirms EY Law Hungary exists as a ranked practice and is the entry point for locating its (presumably subscription-gated) alert channel.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Hungarian Public Procurement Bulletin, daily signed PDF issues)
why_relevant: Legally mandated official gazette of Hungarian public procurement. Every national-threshold notice from state banks' owners, MÁK, ministries, municipalities and state-owned companies buying payment/banking IT (számlavezetés, POS terminál, pénzforgalmi rendszer) appears here, including CPV codes, budget, award and delivery deadlines. Daily issues are published as signed PDFs (e.g. KE-2025-159.pdf), making bulk longitudinal collection feasible.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA) – notice search interface, Közbeszerzési Hatóság
why_relevant: Structured, queryable central register of procurement notices and contracts (including below-threshold summaries). Supports saved searches with daily e-mail alerts — a ready-made monitoring channel for keywords like 'pénzforgalmi', 'kártyaelfogadás', 'core banking', 'terminál'.

source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer, public notice board (hirdetmények)
why_relevant: The mandatory end-to-end platform where Hungarian contracting authorities run procedures; the public 'hirdetmények' view exposes live calls and, crucially, the procurement documentation (közbeszerzési dokumentáció, műszaki leírás) that contains the actual technical/compliance requirements driving payment-system change. Structured search was upgraded in June 2024.

source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ Supplement), Hungary above-threshold notices
why_relevant: All Hungarian above-threshold contracts (services ~EUR 140k+, and utilities/works thresholds) must be published here in a standardised eForms structure, in English as well as Hungarian. This is the cleanest machine-readable route to large state banking/payments IT tenders and their award values and deadlines.

source_name: TED Developer Docs / TED Open Data (Search API, SPARQL endpoint, bulk XML)
why_relevant: Documents the exact programmatic access routes to TED (REST search API, notice XML bulk packages, SPARQL). Turns the TED source above from manual browsing into an automatable long-term collection pipeline.

source_name: Opentender.eu – Hungary country portal (Government Transparency Institute)
why_relevant: Cleaned, harmonised and analysable version of Hungarian procurement data, combining TED with the national Közbeszerzési Hatóság portal to also cover below-threshold contracts. Useful for buyer/supplier concentration analysis and for spotting recurring payment-systems vendors to state buyers.

source_name: openprocurements.com Hungary (hu.openprocurements.com) – buyer-indexed tender aggregator
why_relevant: Provides per-buyer landing pages (e.g. Magyar Államkincstár, NISZ Zrt., BKK) that aggregate that authority's tenders over time — a fast way to build a buyer watchlist and see historical cadence of e.g. 'Pénzforgalmi számlavezetés' procurements.

source_name: Magyar Államkincstár (MÁK) – Üvegzseb / közbeszerzési terv page
why_relevant: The State Treasury is the single most important public buyer of payments/settlement infrastructure in Hungary. Its annual közbeszerzési terv (procurement plan) is a forward-looking signal published before notices appear, revealing planned system changes 6-12 months ahead.

source_name: MÁK – decentralised municipal account-keeping (decentralizált önkormányzati számlavezetés) programme page
why_relevant: A policy shift explicitly dated from 1 October 2025 that changes who keeps Hungarian municipal payment accounts. This is the demand driver behind a wave of municipal számlavezetés tenders and directly determines which banks/PSPs compete for public-sector payment flows.

source_name: Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség (DKÜ) Zrt. – central government IT procurement body
why_relevant: Under Government Decree 301/2018 (XII.27) most state bodies must route IT procurement exclusively through DKÜ. Any state-sector banking/payments IT buy therefore passes through DKÜ's framework agreements — making DKÜ a mandatory gatekeeper and an early indicator of state IT demand and of which vendors hold framework positions.

source_name: KEF – Központosított Közbeszerzési Portál (kozbeszerzes.gov.hu)
why_relevant: The centralised public procurement system portal (keretmegállapodások / KM framework agreements) through which many state entities buy hardware and services, including terminals and IT equipment. KM numbers (e.g. KM08) appear directly in state contract documents, so the portal explains the contracting route behind many awards.

source_name: Magyar Posta Zrt. – Beszerzések, pályázatok (procurement & tenders page)
why_relevant: Magyar Posta is a state-owned entity and a major payments actor (postal payment orders, cash handling, agent banking for a partner bank). Its own procurement page carries calls that are not always duplicated cleanly in the gazette, and reveals planned modernisation of postal payment and counter systems.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) – Közbeszerzés / közérdekű gazdálkodási adatok
why_relevant: The central bank is itself a contracting authority under the Kbt. Its procurements cover supervisory reporting systems, payment-system oversight tooling and cash infrastructure — a direct read on regulator-side system change. The published contract annexes also state MNB's standard IT contractual requirements.

source_name: NISZ Nemzeti Infokommunikációs Szolgáltató Zrt. – Közbeszerzési információk & Közadat
why_relevant: NISZ operates the state's shared infocommunication infrastructure that public payment and e-government services run on. It publishes full annual közbeszerzési terv PDFs and the actual signed contracts (szerződések), giving unusually granular visibility into scope, price and delivery deadlines.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) – decisions database
why_relevant: Remedy-procedure decisions expose contested requirements in banking/payments tenders — e.g. a D.677/2024 decision touching credit-institution IT system development reference criteria. These documents reveal specification detail, bidder identities and the real technical bar, and they flag procurements at risk of delay.

source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – online services & databases hub
why_relevant: Single index page enumerating all official procurement databases and online services (notice search, contract database, KDB decisions, CPV code lists, registers). The most efficient snowball hub for discovering further authoritative endpoints in this cell.

source_name: Átlátszó (atlatszo.hu) – Közpénz investigative reporting on centralised IT procurement
why_relevant: Investigative outlet that reconstructs pricing and vendor patterns in DKÜ-routed state IT procurement (e.g. Aug 2024 piece on state bodies overpaying under centralised IT procurement). Useful as an interpretive/critical layer that surfaces contracts and anomalies not obvious from the raw notices.

source_name: NAV (Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal) – közzétételi lista, megkötött szerződések
why_relevant: The tax authority is a large public buyer whose systems touch payment acceptance, online cash registers and e-invoicing/e-payment interfaces. Its published contract archive (organised by KM framework and year) gives concrete evidence of vendors and delivery deadlines in tax-side payment infrastructure.

source_name: TenderHelp Hungary – tendering interfaces guide (HU/EN)
why_relevant: Bilingual practitioner guide explaining EKR mechanics, registration, and the relationship between EKR, Közbeszerzési Értesítő and TED. Useful for correctly designing the collection method and understanding what is and is not publicly visible without registration.
